title: Тайный перекур и заказ куропаток  (A Secret Smoke Break and Ordering Partridges)

segments.t: At the hospital, Chef Barinov sneaks a forbidden cigarette until a sudden wave of dizziness proves his neighbor right about following doctors' orders. Back at Claude Monet, Max lures Nastya toward the walk-in refrigerator by claiming he urgently needs four partridges.
Ну вот, что я и говорил.
Две куропатки  это просто не дело.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Smoking is forbidden in the hospital.' Max brings out the contrast between 'the hospital' and 'to smoke' in a few short words.
'And what did I tell you?' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'talk' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
'Excuse me, that is amazing.' Notice how Russian expresses 'excuse me' and 'incredible' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Is everything all right?' Max brings out the contrast between 'all' and 'order' in a few short words.
'I am feeling a little dizzy.' Notice how Russian expresses 'for me' and 'is spinning' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
Ну вот, что я и говорил.
'Well, there you go, just like I said.' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'talk' without extra filler words.
'Good job, punk.' The grammar packs 'well done' and 'Rump' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'You have to use your head.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'at' and finishing on 'to think'. Vika answers right away.
'No, no, no.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'there is no' and 'there is no' in a few short words.
Две куропатки  это просто не дело.
'Two partridges simply will not do.' The meaning hinges on 'two' working together with 'matter' in spoken Russian.
'Four at the very minimum.' Notice how Russian expresses 'four' and 'at least' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
'All right then.' Vika anchors the line on 'come on', while 'fine' completes the thought.
'Okay, four it is.' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'four' without extra filler words. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
Ну вот, что я и говорил.
Две куропатки  это просто не дело.
